info.desc: 1000 gecs is the debut studio album and successor to 100 gec’s first eponymous EP. Released in early 2019, the album was positively received due to its aggressive production and wide variety of catchy vocal cadences. The critical success of 1000 gecs extends to multiple year-end lists, with Pitchfork ranking the album as the 42nd best of the year, Jon Pareles of the New York Times citing it as the 10th best, and Noisey declaring it as the best of the year. .

podcast.body: Released in 2019, this album by 100 gecs showcases their exaggerated approach to pop music, becoming a significant work within the Hyperpop genre. "squeezing out an album called 1000 Gecks in 2019."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

podcast.body: This debut album is described as a "sonic collapse" that draws influences from trap, EDM, dubstep, J-Pop, and even monophonic mobile phone melodies. All of this is passed through an autotune filter and enveloped in an absolutely colorful and "chiclosas" (chewing gum-like) aesthetic. Far from being just a joke, the album resonates surprisingly seriously, encapsulating the essence of hyperpop as a genre where anything goes, and its impact has been enormous. "Un colasso honoro que recoge influencias del trap, el EDM, el DAFSTEP, el J-POP y hasta melodías monofónicas de teléfonas móviles."
